logline: Three women in their late thirties navigate rival web portal empires and the romantic entanglements that arrive on the side - a portrait of ambition, power, and desire in digital-age Seoul.

bollymeter.basis: A rare K-drama that places professional women's ambitions front and centre without flattening them into romance vehicles; Im Soo-jung, Lee Da-hee, and Jeon Hye-jin make the portal rivalry crackle with the same intensity as the personal entanglements.

seasons.review_body: Search: WWW arrived on tvN in June 2019 as a workplace drama with an unusually honest premise: three women past 35 running competing internet portals, whose romantic subplots are secondary to the professional war they are waging. Writer Kwon Do-eun and directors Jung Ji-hyun and Kwon Young-il give each of the three protagonists - Bae Ta-mi, Cha Hyeon, and Song Ga-kyeong - a distinct relationship to power and compromise. The portal companies Unicon and Barro function as near-satirical mirrors of the real Korean internet duopoly, and the drama makes the algorithm politics feel genuinely consequential. Im Soo-jung's nomination for Top Excellence at the 12th Korea Drama Awards acknowledged a performance that grounds the show's ambitions. The romance arcs are more formulaic, but the central argument - that ambition in a woman is not a disorder to be cured by love - is stated and maintained with unusual consistency for the genre.

episode_reviews.spoiler_free: A confident premiere that introduces all three women at the top of their professional games and sets the portal rivalry in motion with corporate-thriller briskness.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Bae Ta-mi's board meeting entrance - the show's thesis statement about women and boardroom authority delivered through staging alone.
